recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is recommended for FHIR-3547 unless a future work group decision changes maxLength semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-3547 was a Published FHIR-core StructureDefinition change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking whether ElementDefinition.maxLength described the shortest or longest length. The approved motion revised the definition to describe the maximum length in characters permitted in conformant instances and expected to be supported by conformant consumers, with an implementation note that receivers are not required to reject longer instances and should handle truncation carefully.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied in git commit 0f64975a83 ({#3547} - fix definition of maxLength), the git-svn import of SVN revision 3420 referenced by the Jira comments. That commit replaced the old shortest-length wording in source/datatypes/elementdefinition.xml with the approved maximum-length definition and added the receiver/truncation note.
additional_context: ElementDefinition remains an active current-build type in source/fhir.ini. Later maxLength commits refined primitive-type scope and date applicability without reversing the FHIR-3547 maximum-length semantics. Confluence, Zulip, and related Jira searches found no conflicting community or Jira record.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current active source already contains the approved maximum-length definition and implementation note, and a current source search found no remaining shortest-length or longest-length wording that would recreate the original ambiguity.
